items.title: Category with translation
items.strategy: Define an additive category equipped with a specified additive autoequivalence [1] and a specified quasi-inverse [-1]; do not derive either choice from an equivalence class of functors.

items.title: Triangle in a category with translation
items.strategy: Define a triangle as X to Y to Z to X[1], retaining all three objects and all three displayed morphisms as data.

items.title: Morphism and isomorphism of triangles
items.strategy: Require three maps and all three commuting squares, including the square into the translated first object; define an isomorphism componentwise.

items.title: Rotation of a triangle
items.strategy: Fix left rotation as Y to Z to X[1] to -f[1] Y[1], and define the inverse rotation using the supplied quasi-inverse so every later sign has one convention.

items.title: Distinguished triangle
items.strategy: Specify a class of triangles intended to satisfy the Verdier axioms, reserving the synonym exact triangle until those axioms have been imposed.

items.title: Triangulated-category axiom TR1
items.strategy: State closure under isomorphism, completion of every map to a distinguished triangle, and the identity triangle X to X to 0 to X[1].

items.title: Triangulated-category axiom TR2
items.strategy: State that a triangle is distinguished exactly when its declared signed left rotation is distinguished.

items.title: Triangulated-category axiom TR3
items.strategy: State completion of a commutative square on first maps to a morphism of triangles, explicitly asserting existence without a uniqueness clause.

items.title: Triangulated-category axiom TR4 (octahedral)
items.strategy: For composable maps and chosen distinguished triangles for each map and their composite, state the typed octahedron, its fourth distinguished face, and its signed commutativity conditions.

items.title: Triangulated category
items.strategy: Package a category with translation and a distinguished class satisfying TR1 through TR4, retaining the class and translation as specified structure.

items.title: The triangulated rotation-sign convention
items.strategy: Record that the library places the minus sign on the final map of left rotation, and translate every imported cone and long-exact-Hom formula to this convention.

items.title: Zero and split triangles are distinguished
items.strategy: Rotate the identity triangle to obtain the zero triangle, derive finite-biproduct closure by the TR3 matrix argument and representable exactness, and take the biproduct of identity and zero triangles.

items.title: Distinguished triangles are closed under shifts and both rotations
items.strategy: Iterate TR2 three times to obtain the positive translate up to the prescribed signs, use the equivalence in both directions for every integral shift, and identify inverse rotation.

items.title: Homological functor on a triangulated category
items.strategy: Define an additive covariant functor to an abelian category by exactness on each distinguished triangle, and display the shifted long exact continuation.

items.title: Cohomological functor on a triangulated category
items.strategy: Define an additive contravariant functor by the oppositely oriented exact sequence and make the translated long continuation explicit.

items.title: Representable Hom functors on a triangulated category are homological or cohomological
items.strategy: Use TR1 to compare with the zero triangle, TR3 to factor any map killed by the next arrow, and rotation to obtain exactness at every translated term; pass to the opposite category for the contravariant variance.

items.title: Long exact Hom sequences of a distinguished triangle
items.strategy: Apply the two representable functors to a distinguished triangle and print both variances with all shifts and the rotation-sign convention visible.

items.title: The triangulated five lemma
items.strategy: Apply Hom from an arbitrary object to the morphism of distinguished triangles, use the established long exact sequences and the five lemma, then invoke the representable zero-detection argument.

items.title: Two isomorphism components of a morphism of triangles force the third
items.strategy: Apply the triangulated five lemma after rotating as necessary so that the unknown component occupies the five-lemma position.

items.title: A map is zero exactly when the corresponding representable map vanishes
items.strategy: Evaluate the natural transformation induced by a map at the identity of its source for the converse, and use composition for the forward implication.

items.title: A distinguished triangle with zero first map is split
items.strategy: Use representable exactness to obtain a section and a preliminary retraction, correct the latter by t-ts h so its cross term vanishes, and verify the two biproduct matrices are inverse.

items.title: A distinguished triangle splits exactly when one connecting map vanishes
items.strategy: Rotate the triangle to reduce each possible vanishing map to the first-map case, and translate the resulting splitting into equivalent section and retraction conditions.

items.title: The cone object of a map is unique up to nonunique isomorphism
items.strategy: Use TR3 to obtain a morphism between two completions of the same first map and the two-isomorphisms proposition to make its third component invertible; retain no claim of canonical choice or uniqueness.

items.title: The octahedral axiom gives a triangle relating the cones of f, g, and gf
items.strategy: Choose distinguished triangles for f, g, and their composite, then read the fourth distinguished face of TR4 as the triangle relating the three cone objects.

items.title: Exact functor between triangulated categories
items.strategy: Define an additive functor equipped with a specified natural translation isomorphism which carries distinguished triangles to distinguished triangles, including compatibility at the final arrow.

items.title: A translation-compatible natural isomorphism of exact functors respects triangles
items.strategy: Use naturality on the first two arrows and the stipulated compatibility with the translation isomorphisms to verify the final square, hence a morphism of image triangles.

items.title: Triangulated subcategory
items.strategy: Define a full additive subcategory closed under translations and two-out-of-three on distinguished triangles, with the inherited distinguished class made explicit.

items.title: Thick subcategory
items.strategy: Define a thick subcategory as a triangulated subcategory also closed under direct summands, spelling this out as closure under a section-retraction pair.

items.title: The total kernel of a cohomological functor is thick
items.strategy: For objects whose every translate is annihilated, use the long exact sequence for two-out-of-three and additivity to show every retract of an annihilated object is annihilated.

items.title: The full subcategory of acyclic complexes is thick in the homotopy category
items.strategy: Use the cone long exact sequence for two-out-of-three, shift-invariance of homology, and degreewise finite biproducts to show acyclic complexes form a thick subcategory of K(A).

items.title: Standard cone triangle in the homotopy category
items.strategy: Pass the established chain-level cone triangle to K(A), translating its final map to the fixed [1] convention and preserving the declared sign.

items.title: Distinguished cone triangle in the homotopy category
items.strategy: Declare a triangle in K(A) distinguished when it is isomorphic to a standard cone triangle, so the definition is invariant under the quotient by homotopy.

items.title: Cone triangles satisfy TR1
items.strategy: Complete each chain map with its cone and show the identity cone is contractible, hence zero in K(A); then use isomorphism closure from the definition.

items.title: Cone triangles satisfy TR2 with the declared rotation sign
items.strategy: Compute the cone of the cone inclusion, split off the contractible identity cone, and identify the remaining projection and connecting map with the signed left rotation.

items.title: Cone triangles satisfy TR3
items.strategy: Represent a homotopy-commutative square by chain maps and a specified homotopy, insert that homotopy as the off-diagonal cone-map entry, and verify the triangle squares in the homotopy category.

items.title: Cone triangles satisfy the octahedral axiom
items.strategy: Use the explicit three-cone matrices for composable chain maps, verify their chain maps and homotopy equivalence, and identify the fourth face with the signed standard cone triangle.

items.title: The homotopy category of an abelian category is triangulated
items.strategy: Combine the inherited shift autoequivalence, the cone-triangle distinguished class, and the four separately proved TR1--TR4 lemmas.

items.title: Homology is a homological functor on the homotopy category
items.strategy: Identify the long exact sequence of a standard cone triangle with the existing cone sequence and its connector, then transport exactness along isomorphisms of triangles.

items.title: An additive functor on abelian categories induces an exact functor on homotopy categories
items.strategy: Apply the additive functor degreewise, use preservation of finite biproducts and zero morphisms to compare cones and shifts, and obtain the required translation isomorphism and image-triangle property without assuming abelian exactness.

items.title: A quasi-isomorphism has an acyclic cone in the triangulated language
items.strategy: Invoke the established chain-level cone criterion and reinterpret its cone as the third object of the standard distinguished triangle in K(A).

items.title: The third map in a morphism of triangles is unique
items.strategy: Refute the asserted uniqueness by separating TR3's existence clause from uniqueness and constructing two distinct completions of one zero square.

items.title: Cones form a functor in every triangulated category
items.strategy: Refute by observing that TR1 and TR3 provide cone objects and comparison maps only noncanonically; a functorial choice needs additional enhancement data.

items.title: A triangle is distinguished whenever the three composites vanish
items.strategy: Refute with a concrete zero-composite triangle in K(A) that is not isomorphic to any standard cone triangle, showing that vanishing composites are only necessary.

items.title: The octahedral axiom is the associativity of composition
items.strategy: Refute by reading TR4 as a comparison between chosen cone triangles of f, g, and gf, rather than the ordinary category axiom for composing arrows.

items.title: Every triangulated subcategory is thick
items.strategy: In the bounded homotopy category of finitely generated free abelian groups, take the full subcategory of complexes with even Euler characteristic. Verify shift and triangle two-out-of-three closure from the cone formula, then observe that the even-Euler object Z[0] direct-sum Z[0] has the odd-Euler summand Z[0], so this triangulated subcategory is not thick.

items.title: The rotation of a distinguished triangle has no sign
items.strategy: Refute against the fixed convention: the final arrow of the left rotation is -f[1], and omitting it conflicts with the chosen cone and long-exact-Hom signs.

items.title: The split distinguished triangle
items.strategy: Write the canonical biproduct maps for X and Y and check the split-triangle criterion together with the declared zero connecting morphism.

items.title: The cone triangle of multiplication by m
items.strategy: Take multiplication by a nonzero integer m on a stalk complex, write its cone and its three maps, and recognize the resulting standard distinguished triangle in K(Ab).

items.title: The long exact Hom sequence of a cone triangle
items.strategy: Apply Hom from a fixed stalk complex to the multiplication-by-m cone triangle and display consecutive maps, including the shifted connecting morphism.

items.title: An octahedron for two composable maps of stalk complexes
items.strategy: Use multiplication by m and n on stalk complexes, identify the three cone triangles for m, n, and nm, and exhibit the fourth octahedral face through the concrete three-cone construction.

items.title: The thick subcategory of acyclic complexes
items.strategy: Apply the established thickness proposition to an acyclic cone triangle and identify the shifts and direct summands that remain acyclic.

items.title: A three-term zero-composite diagram that is not distinguished
items.strategy: Use stalk complexes to form a triangle with all three composites zero, then compare the noncontractible cone obstruction to show it cannot be a standard distinguished triangle.

items.title: Nonuniqueness of a TR3 completion
items.strategy: Choose a split triangle with a nonzero compatible endomorphism in the third component and construct two distinct completions of the same first square.
